decisions.executionNote: Lift left arm in elbow-up approach toward the cup in its workspace; right arm stays at origin. Cup location estimated from calibrated head image.
Advance above the left cup while pitching gripper downward, retaining elbow-up continuity.
Orient left fingers nearly vertical above cup; approach remains clear of rim while checking wrist alignment.
Center over cup and descend slowly with open jaws. Final pitch makes fingers vertical; monitor depth before closing.
Settle fingers just below the cup rim, then close gradually. Retention will be checked with a small lift rather than inferred from gripper command.
Lift closed left gripper to check cup retention. Begin elbow-up right approach to bring vase nearer the center without crossing arms.
Cup is visibly retained with seven balls. Raise it slightly while right arm approaches above vase, keeping both arms on their own sides.
Keep cup upright and retained; advance right gripper above vase with increasing downward pitch.
Cup appears to have slipped back onto table. Reopen left jaws and approach its right rim for a wall pinch, while finishing right-arm alignment above vase.
Pinch the cup's right rim with left jaws and the vase's right rim with right jaws. Avoid squeezing across the cup center, which did not retain it.
Small vertical lift with both jaws closed to visually verify rim-pinches before transport.
Cup rim pinch appears retained. Right grasp missed the vase; reopen and offset outward to straddle its right rim, then close below the lip.
Lower right fingers another two centimeters below the flared vase lip before closing; left holds cup steady.
Allow right closure to settle, then gently lift to test whether the vase follows. Keep the cup closed and upright.
Right fingers closed outside the vase. Reopen, shift inward and back to align with its right wall, and descend farther under the rim. Left cup remains retained.
Pause to finish right rim closure at the contact-limited height, then test retention by lifting slightly. Avoid further downward pressure.
Correct right rim alignment outward using the wrist view and straighten the fingers vertically before another gentle closure.
Leave vase standing and withdraw right arm. Raise retained cup and approach the vase from the left; plan a leftward tilt with cup extending right of the left wrist, without crossing arms.
Position cup above and left of the vase while keeping tilt below pouring angle. Withdraw right arm farther to clear the pouring path.
Replan after continuity rejection: smaller inward steps and lower wrist to preserve extension margin. Cup remains below pouring tilt; right retracts.
Raise cup for vase clearance while increasing tilt toward a pouring pose. Keep left wrist in left workspace; cup swings right over the vase as right arm retracts.
Bring the cup's low lip over the vase opening while slowly approaching horizontal. Keep grasp closed and leave right arm clear of the falling-ball path.
Slowly tilt past horizontal with low lip aligned above vase; watch for ball release. Finish returning the unobstructing right arm to origin.
Balls are visibly dropping into the vase opening. Keep the low lip aligned and let the remaining balls roll out with only a slight additional tilt.
Cup appears empty. Withdraw toward the left and begin restoring upright orientation, checking the cleared scene for any balls outside the vase.
Continue restoring the empty cup upright and move back toward its left-side placement location. Right arm remains at origin.
Restore cup upright for safe placement. RGB now shows balls outside the vase, so transfer is not complete and will require recovery after setting the cup down.
Lower the cup toward its original tabletop position while completing upright rotation; keep jaws closed until it is supported.
Release the cup upright on the table and clear it. Several spilled balls are visible; prepare a careful individual recovery rather than claiming completion.
Move the open left gripper above the nearby spilled-ball cluster for visual alignment and individual pickup.
Align over the nearest spilled ball using head geometry and wrist feedback, then approach table height slowly with jaws open.
Fine-center the nearest ball between the fingertips and descend cautiously toward its tabletop height, keeping the other balls undisturbed.
Table contact limits further descent. Relieve pressure, align the ball with fingertip tips, and close gently for an individual pickup.
A ball is visibly between the closed fingertips. Lift it gently and begin orienting the hand so the ball can be released vertically above the vase without crossing arms.
The ball was not retained. Reopen and align vertically over a nearby spilled ball for a slower pinch and lift, avoiding rotation during the retention test.
Fine-adjust over the left ball of the close pair. Place it farther between the finger pads rather than at their leading tips, with a slow descent.
Choose the isolated ball just left of center to avoid pinching two together. Approach slowly with a partially narrowed gap, preserving the ball within the pad region.
Two balls are between the pads. Relieve table contact slightly, finish closing, and make only a tiny vertical retention test without rotation.
A ball is centered between closed pads. Test retention with a slow two-centimeter vertical lift only, keeping orientation fixed.
Ball stays fixed between pads during the lift. Raise it clear and gradually swing fingertips toward the vase while keeping the left wrist left of center.
The sphere was lost during wrist rotation. Clear the left arm and approach the isolated right-side ball with the right arm, allowing transport to the vase with fixed wrist orientation.
Advance right arm above the isolated right-side sphere and pitch downward. Left stays clear in its own workspace.
Finish vertical right-gripper alignment above the isolated sphere. Keep ample clearance before descending.
Descend over the isolated sphere while positioning it deeper between the right finger pads. Keep wrist orientation fixed for pickup and transport.
Center the isolated ball between the right pads, descend the last small distance, and close gradually while holding orientation fixed.
Allow the right pads to finish closing around the ball, then test with a four-millimeter vertical lift only.
The head view suggests the right fingertips were still above the sphere. Reopen and descend farther in small increments to reach its height before another closure.
Descent is contact-limited. Relieve pressure and move back so the ball lies at the low fingertip region instead of behind the pads; straighten the right wrist.
Ball is now at the fingertip contact region. Descend about one centimeter and close slowly without translating it.
Sphere is visibly between the right pads. Test retention with a slow vertical lift, keeping orientation fixed and jaws closed.
Ball remains fixed between right pads. Raise it vertically toward clearance above the vase, with no wrist rotation.
Continue lifting the retained sphere to clear the vase lip before moving inward. Maintain the successful fixed wrist orientation.
Translate the retained right-hand ball toward the vase while lifting slightly above its rim; no wrist rotation.
Move the retained ball inward and forward above the vase. Keep clearance and inspect wrist alignment before release.
Replan after continuity guard with smaller increments and lower height to regain configuration margin while retaining the ball above the vase rim.
Move the retained ball slowly forward and slightly inward toward the visible vase opening; inspect alignment before opening the pads.
After the continuity stop, lower slightly while advancing in submillimeter increments to regain configuration margin and bring the sphere just inside the vase lip.
Advance the retained sphere a final short distance past the near rim, maintaining wrist orientation and small joint-continuous increments before release.
Sphere is now inside the visible vase rim. Release it in place using a modest jaw opening, keeping both wrists stationary after the continuity interruption.
The released sphere disappeared into the vase opening. Withdraw the right fingertips upward and back, increasing configuration margin before collecting the next right-side sphere.
Previous withdrawal was rejected before movement. Retry with one-quarter-size increments from the unchanged pose to preserve IK continuity.
Continue withdrawing clear of the vase rim with the empty right gripper, then prepare to collect a nearby sphere in the right workspace.
Clear the vase on its left without crossing the centerline, then begin descending toward the next right-workspace sphere. Keep wrist orientation fixed.
Replan from the continuity stop: withdraw backward and slightly downward with much smaller inward motion, restoring elbow-up configuration margin before the next pickup.
